draft.title: Enlargements
card: An enlargement changes the size of a shape but not its shape. Every length is multiplied by the same number, called the scale factor.
Angles stay the same. Only lengths change, so the new shape has the same look as the original, just bigger or smaller.
A scale factor above 1 makes the shape bigger. A scale factor between 0 and 1 makes it smaller.
A rectangle is 4 cm by 6 cm. Enlarge it with scale factor 3. The new sides are \(4 \times 3 = 12\) cm and \(6 \times 3 = 18\) cm, and every corner is still \(90^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: Multiply every length by the scale factor. Angles do not change.

a.q: A triangle has angles of \(40^{\circ}\), \(60^{\circ}\) and \(80^{\circ}\). It is enlarged with scale factor 2. What are the angles of the new triangle?
a.why: An enlargement keeps every angle the same, so the angles are still \(40^{\circ}\), \(60^{\circ}\) and \(80^{\circ}\). Doubling them would give angles that add to \(360^{\circ}\), which is impossible for a triangle.
a.clue: Does an enlargement change angles or only lengths?

b.q: Mia's photo is 8 cm wide and 5 cm tall. She enlarges it with scale factor 2.5. What are the new width and height?
b.why: Every length is multiplied by 2.5: \(8 \times 2.5 = 20\) and \(5 \times 2.5 = 12.5\). Adding 2.5 to each side is tempting, but that changes the shape, because the lengths are not all scaled by the same multiple.
b.clue: Multiply both sides by the scale factor.
